ticket.title: miter deps calls a dependency unused when it is only referenced by a fully-qualified path
ticket.description:
Found the hard way during GB-201: batten-core declares `regex` and uses it as `regex::escape(id)` in src/grammar/regex.rs with no `use regex;` statement. The scanner reports the dependency as unused, and I acted on that report by demoting it to [dev-dependencies] - which failed to compile. The gate caught it, regex was restored, and the incidence is recorded in the batten commit.

Root cause: `collect_crate_imports` collects imports (use statements and `crate::`/`mod` paths), not qualified references. A dependency reached only through `extern_crate::item` therefore looks dead. That is the same class of over-reporting as GB-199 (fixture strings counted as references) but in the opposite direction, and it produces a false positive that a careful operator will act on destructively.

SCOPE: while stripping literals and comments, also recognise `ident::` paths in expression position as a reference, so `regex::escape` counts. Then re-measure GB-201 - the current 34 unused includes at least this one false positive, and the real number is lower.

verification_receipt.summary: A local module no longer hides a dependency of the same name. collect_crate_imports filtered any root ident that matched a module name declared in the crate, so batten-core mod regex; hid the regex crate and regex::escape(id) was discarded - I acted on that report by demoting the dependency, which failed to compile. The rule is now name plus context: hide only when the ident is not a declared dependency, since a local module named like a dependency is rare and the alternative failure mode is a destructive purge recommendation. Re-measured: unused declarations 34 -> 30, and the four that disappeared were all this same collision - batten-core/regex, miter-engine/hcl, rabbet-core/parquet and outfeed-core/semver. parquet had been flagged for manual review precisely because deleting it looked wrong; it was a false positive. Diagnosis recorded: three hypotheses (path scan, stripper, walk) were each refuted by a test, and only an instrumented run of the collector showed the missing key. Gate: clippy -D warnings, 181 tests, fmt green.
